claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is an as-cast, coarse-grained material.
Cold rolling to 50% thickness reduction introduces deformation-induced defects.
Cold rolling followed by annealing at 1000°C for 1 hour will produce a fine-grained HfNbTaTiZr microstructure.
Reducing grain size increases the volume fraction or density of grain boundaries.
Grain boundaries in refined HfNbTaTiZr act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The refined grain-boundary network alters local stress distributions.
Increasing the grain-boundary density modifies lattice-vibration modes and anharmonic vibrational behavior.
The fine-grained alloy will have higher yield strength than the as-cast coarse-grained alloy.
The fine-grained alloy will have a higher elastic modulus than the as-cast coarse-grained alloy.
The fine-grained alloy will exhibit a thermal-expansion coefficient or profile distinct from that of the as-cast alloy.
Deformation-induced defects other than grain boundaries may contribute to the measured responses.
The predicted mechanical, elastic, and thermal-expansion differences should remain observable from room temperature to 1000°C.
Above 1000°C, phase instabilities or other phenomena may dominate the response.
The controlled comparison consists of identically composed processed and as-cast HfNbTaTiZr samples tested over the same temperature range.
TEM or EBSD measurements of grain size, dislocation density, and grain-boundary characteristics are intended to separate grain-boundary effects from other defect contributions.
Yield strength, elastic modulus, thermal expansion, grain size, and dislocation density will be measured at multiple temperatures between room temperature and 1000°C.

The hypothesis is falsified if the processed sample lacks statistically significant strength and modulus improvements, lacks a distinct thermal-expansion profile, or lacks the predicted increase in grain-boundary density.
